h1: The 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaners for Jewelry of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Jewelry Ultrasonic Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 jewelry ultrasonic cleaners compared on frequency, power and gentle settings, from 350 ml tubs to an 800 ml dual-transducer.
summary: The VisiClean 800 ml dual-transducer is the jewelry cleaner with the most headroom: it takes bracelets and several rings at once. The LifeBasis 600 ml adds a degas step and long preset, and the onlikin lets you drop to a gentler power level for mixed collections. The Magnasonic is the dependable budget standard, and the OSLTWI and KUNPHY are compact, simple tubs for light use.
intro: Most jewelry that goes into an ultrasonic tank comes out fine, and some does not. Opals, pearls, emeralds and treated stones can craze or cloud, and glued or fracture-filled pieces can loosen. The machine rarely causes the damage; the buyer who runs a gentle setting for the wrong stone or leaves a ring in for ten minutes does. The best jewelry cleaner is the one that lets you stay conservative.

We ranked six tubs on the Primea framework, weighting adjustable power and short preset timers above raw wattage. Frequency, tank length for bracelets, noise and warranty support all feed the score, since a jewelry cleaner lives on a bathroom counter and is used for minutes at a time, not hours.

products.name: VisiClean 800 ml Dual Transducer Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.verdict: Two transducers and an 800 ml tank that handle bracelets and several rings at a time.
products.description:
The VisiClean pairs two transducers at 42,000 Hz with an 800 ml (27 oz) stainless tank, five presets and a built-in cooling fan. The tank is the largest here, so a tennis bracelet or a stack of rings loads without overlapping.

It wins because jewelry cleans better when pieces sit apart, and the dual transducers keep cavitation consistent across that wider floor. The Magnasonic below uses the same frequency but a smaller tank, and the 350 ml tubs force you to clean in rounds.

Buy it if you own bracelets, watch bands or a large ring collection. The $50 to $100 price is the highest in the group, and the stronger output means shorter cycles on delicate gold chains.
products.idealFor: Owners of bracelets, watch bands and big ring collections.
products.skipIf: You only own a few rings and want something pocket-size.

products.name: LifeBasis 600 ml 45kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner
products.verdict: A 45 kHz tub with an automatic 20 second degas and five timers up to 600 seconds.
products.description:
Transducer power is 35W at 45,000 Hz, the tank is 600 ml of SUS 304 steel, and presets run 90, 180, 300, 480 and 600 seconds. A 20 second degas step clears air from fresh solution, and a cooling fan keeps the housing from heating on long runs.

The higher frequency is the reason it sits second: finer bubbles mean gentler scrubbing, which suits soft gold and detailed settings. It trails the VisiClean on tank size and total output, so it clears light tarnish and oils but not heavy buildup.

Choose it for day-to-day cleaning of everyday pieces. The caveat is the long 600 second preset, which is more than most gemstones should see at one stretch.
products.idealFor: Jewelry owners who want automatic degassing and flexible timers.
products.skipIf: You need to clean a long bracelet in one go.

products.name: onlikin 35W 45kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 20 oz
products.verdict: Three adjustable power levels and a quiet tub under 38 dB for mixed jewelry collections.
products.description:
Power is 35W with three levels you can pick between, frequency is 45,000 Hz, and the 20 oz tank is 304 stainless. Five timers run 90, 180, 300, 420 and 480 seconds, and the listing quotes noise under 38 dB.

The adjustable power is what earns third place. Few jewelry tubs let you drop below full output, and that matters when a drawer holds gold, silver and a few delicate pieces. It ranks under the LifeBasis because it lacks a degas cycle, and under the VisiClean for tank size.

Buy it for a mixed collection and a quiet counter. The caveat is that its top power is still only 35W, so it is a maintenance cleaner, not a restoration tool.
products.idealFor: Owners of mixed jewelry who want a lighter setting and a quiet tub.

products.name: Magnasonic 20oz Stainless Steel Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.verdict: Five cycles from quick to deep, a digital display and a basket for $25 to $50.
products.description:
A 600 ml (20 oz) stainless tank, 42,000 Hz output, digital display and timer, five cycles from quick to deep, and a basket in the box. It is the most widely recommended entry unit in the category, and the spec sheet shows why.

It ranks fourth because it does one thing without frills. There is no degas and no power adjustment, so delicate pieces rely on you choosing the short cycle. Against the onlikin it cleans similarly at a similar price, but it gives you no way to reduce output.

Good for rings, chains and glasses. The caveat is the lack of a gentle mode, so keep porous stones out and favor the quick cycle.
products.idealFor: Households that want one dependable machine for jewelry and glasses.
products.skipIf: You own porous or treated stones and want a low-power option.

products.name: OSLTWI 48kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.verdict: The highest frequency here, 48 kHz, in a 0.57 kg tub with a one-touch selector.
products.description:
A 350 ml, 304 stainless tank, two cleaning modes and a one-touch selector make this the most minimal unit in the group. Frequency is 48 kHz, the highest listed, and the whole machine weighs 0.57 kg.

It ranks fifth because tank size is the limit: a bracelet will not lie flat, and larger rings need to be cleaned one at a time. The higher frequency makes it gentle, but that gentleness also means slower work on build-up than the VisiClean or the LifeBasis.

Pick it for rings, studs and light daily cleaning, especially if you travel with it. Pass on it if your collection includes bracelets or chunky pieces.
products.idealFor: People cleaning rings and studs who want a small, simple tub.
products.skipIf: You own bracelets or bulky pieces.

products.name: KUNPHY 46kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.verdict: A single-button, 3-minute fixed cycle at 46 kHz with a one-year quality commitment.
products.description:
The KUNPHY runs one 3-minute cycle at 46,000 Hz in a 350 ml tank, quoted below 45 dB. A single button starts the cycle, and the company offers a one-year quality commitment.

That simplicity is the whole pitch, and the limit as well. You cannot lengthen the cycle for stubborn tarnish and cannot shorten it for a delicate piece, which keeps it behind the OSLTWI's two modes. It also trails the Magnasonic on tank size and basket inclusion.

It makes sense as a first purchase or a gift for someone who just wants clean rings. Skip it if you care about timer control or clean large items regularly.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers and gift givers who want a single-button tub.
products.skipIf: You want to set the cleaning time yourself.

methodology.title: Frequency and gentleness
methodology.description: Higher kHz means finer bubbles and a gentler clean, so we credit 45 kHz and above for delicate stones and soft metals.

methodology.title: Adjustable power and timers
methodology.description: The ability to lower output and choose short cycles protects porous or treated pieces.

methodology.title: Tank capacity for jewelry
methodology.description: Whether a bracelet, chain or several rings fit without touching each other.

methodology.title: Noise and daily use
methodology.description: Operating noise, cooling and weight, because a jewelry cleaner lives on a bathroom counter.

methodology.title: Support and price
methodology.description: Warranty commitments and price bucket relative to features delivered.

whatMatters.detail: Frequency sets bubble size: lower kHz means bigger, harsher bubbles; higher means finer ones. The OSLTWI runs 48 kHz, the LifeBasis and onlikin 45 kHz, the Magnasonic and VisiClean 42,000 Hz. For jewelry, higher is the safer default, but check the listing for the exact number.

A tub that only runs at full power forces you to manage risk with the clock. The onlikin gives three power levels, which is rare at this price. If your collection includes soft or treated stones, look for a power selector or short presets before wattage.

Pieces should not touch each other or the tank walls, or cleaning is uneven. 350 ml fits rings and studs, 600 ml fits chains, 800 ml fits a bracelet. Measure your longest chain, compare it to the tank volume on the listing, and size up if you are close.

Jewelry rarely needs more than a few minutes. Look for short presets such as 90 or 180 seconds. The LifeBasis and onlikin both give five timers, while the KUNPHY has a single 3 minute cycle. More choices let you rinse, inspect and repeat instead of over-running.

Freshly mixed solution has trapped air that dampens cavitation. A degas step runs briefly to clear it before cleaning starts. The LifeBasis automates a 20 second degas. Others require you to run the empty tank briefly. It helps first-minute performance, which matters when cycles are short.

faq.a: You can, but a drop of jewelry solution improves cleaning. The Magnasonic and VisiClean work with plain water for light dust, while heavier buildup benefits from solution. Always rinse and dry after, and never use ammonia on porous stones.

faq.q: What mistake ruins jewelry most often?
faq.a: Running opals, pearls or emeralds. Those stones can craze, cloud or fracture, and no tub here can protect them. Even the gentle onlikin or the 48 kHz OSLTWI should only see solid metal and hard stones like diamond.

faq.q: Is the VisiClean worth it over the Magnasonic?
faq.a: If you clean bracelets or large batches, yes. It adds a second transducer and an 800 ml tank, while the Magnasonic holds 600 ml. For a few rings the Magnasonic does nearly the same work for less money.

faq.q: How do I set up for the first use?
faq.a: Fill to the marked line with water and a few drops of solution, then run the LifeBasis degas or a short empty cycle on the others. Place jewelry in the basket so nothing rests directly on the stainless floor.

faq.q: How long should a cycle be?
faq.a: Start with 90 to 180 seconds and inspect. The LifeBasis and onlikin offer presets at those lengths, while the KUNPHY's fixed 3 minute run suits sturdy metal. Longer runs add little for jewelry and raise risk. Stop, rinse, look at the piece under good light, and only then decide whether it needs another round.

faq.q: Can I clean a watch in these?
faq.a: Only metal bands with the case removed. Water and vibration can damage a movement, even in water-resistant watches. The VisiClean tank is the one here long enough to take a full bracelet band.

finalTake: The VisiClean 800 ml Dual Transducer Ultrasonic Cleaner is the strongest jewelry buy for anyone with bracelets or a growing collection. The LifeBasis adds automation, and the onlikin is the pick when you need control over power. The Magnasonic stays the dependable budget choice, while the OSLTWI and KUNPHY are fine for light, compact use. Whichever you choose, keep porous stones out.
